findings:
FINDINGS OUTSIDE THE CLAIMS

F1 (blocking) — /home/user/fleet/sqlite/src/server/SQLiteStatement.ts:109-113. The comment the unit authored beside its own fix states: "The `finally` reaches the native iterator's own `return` on EVERY exit, the abandoned ones included". That is false. A generator called but never stepped stays in the suspended-start state, so its body never runs: `const it = statement.iterate()` followed by dropping the reference never runs the `finally` at all, and `it.return()` on that unstarted generator completes it without executing the body, so the `finally` does not run there either. Only exits that reach a `yield` — the `break`, early `return`, and throw the same sentence enumerates — are covered. The unit's own row text (conform-sqlite-brief.md:83) names "or simply calling `iterate()` and never stepping it" as one of the abandonment paths, so the comment claims coverage of a case the refuter listed and the code does not reach. Why it matters: this round is repairing prose claims the code contradicts (sqlite-subj-4, -6, -10 are all that class), and the same diff introduces a new one about the very behaviour it changes; .claude/rules/writing.md § Claims and time ("Claim only what the reader can check") and .claude/rules/documentation.md § Parity ("Falsify a prose claim the way you falsify a code claim") both reach a source comment through AGENTS.md § Writing, which governs prose everywhere. What right looks like: replace "on EVERY exit" with "on every exit after the first step", leaving the rest of the sentence, which already scopes itself to a generator completed at its `yield` and to "the stepped native statement". Do not extend the code to finalize a never-stepped iterator in this round — that is a new design decision outside the ruled repair, and the eager native iterator at :82-92 holds no read transaction until it is stepped.

F2 (blocking, with a two-way close) — /home/user/fleet/sqlite/src/server/SQLiteStatement.ts:126-128. The new `finally { native.return?.() }` calls into `node:sqlite` unguarded on the error path. If that call throws, it replaces the in-flight exception, so a `SQLiteError` the wrapper just mapped, or the caller's own error thrown from the `for...of` body, is displaced by a raw native throw — the exact outcome guides/sqlite.md:106 promises never happens ("never escaping raw from the caller's `for...of`"), and the exact masking this package already guards against in the analogous place (src/server/SQLiteDatabase.ts:106-112 wraps the rollback in `try { … } catch {}` with the comment "must never mask the scope's own error"). Reachability is NOT-EVIDENCED by me: this lane runs read-only and cannot execute, and the one error path the suite exercises is proven safe (the mid-stream-fault control at tests/src/server/SQLiteStatement.test.ts:76-82 stayed green after the fix, so `return` did not throw there). The unmeasured path is a caller closing the database inside the loop and then leaving it. What right looks like — either: (a) wrap the call, matching the file's own precedent — `} finally { try { native.return?.() } catch { /* swallowed — finalizing the native iterator must not mask the caller's own error */ } }`; or (b) record the executed reading from `vitest run --project src:server` over a case that runs `for (const row of statement.iterate()) { db.close(); break }` and shows `sqliteErrorCode` returning a mapped code rather than `NOT_SQLITE_ERROR`, and keep the call unguarded on that evidence.

F3 (not blocking; recording gap) — /home/user/scaffold/tmp/units/conform/conform-sqlite-report.md:75. The brief's § Method item 2 requires, for a naming row, "a word-boundary search over the old name, and a second case-insensitive search over its `-s`, `-ed`, and `-ing` inflections". § Sweeps records only the word-boundary form (`grep -rnw "run\|transaction\|SQLiteRunResult"`). I ran the inflection sweep myself over the report's own path list and it reads empty, so claim 3 stands on substance; only the transcription is missing. What right looks like: add the recorded line `grep -rniE "\brun(s|ning)?\b|\btransaction(s|ed|ing)?\b|SQLiteRunResults?"` over the same paths, with its reading, beside the existing sweep.

F4 (blocking; cheap) — the report states counts, which AGENTS.md § Writing bans outright ("NEVER state a count … rows … are such sets. Name the members … Delete a count you find"), and the report is developer prose governed by .claude/rules/writing.md. Sites: report:3 "Two rows are breaking"; report:76 "three hits, all `just` meaning 'only'"; report:145 "Three decisions are recorded"; report:13 "One sentinel spelling remains"; report:24 "One further hit fixed". What right looks like: name the members — "sqlite-subj-1 and sqlite-subj-14 are breaking"; "the `just` hits at src/server/SQLiteDatabase.ts:92, src/server/types.ts:82, and guides/sqlite.md:221 read as 'only'"; "§ Deviations records the decisions on sqlite-subj-7, sqlite-subj-18, and sqlite-subj-3". Fix the stale citation in the same edit: report:76 cites `guides/sqlite.md:217` for the `just` hit, which sits at :221 in the shipped file.

REFERRALS (no verdict from me)

R1 — to the Orchestrator (this round runs no other lane on this question). sqlite-subj-12's ruled repair deleted the `## Methods` preamble clause that named `path` / `connected` / `transacting` as the interface's readonly data members. After it, guides/sqlite.md documents `transacting` at :71 and leaves `path` and `connected` named only inside fences, while .claude/rules/documentation.md § Parity states "Readonly data properties remain in the interface's `## Surface` row" and the `SQLiteDatabase` Surface row at :32 lists methods only. The gap predates this unit (no Surface row ever carried them) and the writer applied the ruling as written, so this is not a defect of the unit; it is a consequence of the ruling that wants a decision before the guide is treated as settled.

R2 — to the Orchestrator. The report's § Deviations item on sqlite-subj-18 leaves README.md:8-10 stating a reading on Node 22.22.2 while package.json:90 declares the floor `>=22.12.0`, so a reader on the floor gets no statement. Settling it needs a second Node on the host, which this lane cannot install and the unit could not reach.

R3 — to the Orchestrator, carried from the writer, verified by me: /home/user/fleet/database/guides/sqlite.md is a byte-identical vendored mirror still carrying `run`, `SQLiteRunResult`, and `transaction` (:58, :81, :92, and the Methods tables). It must be refreshed from the released tree after this package publishes, not hand-edited, and the consumer's own unit carries the nine call-site edits transcribed under § Breaking.

VERDICT: FAIL none; outside the claims: F1, F2, F4
